Hi Sophie — looping in our solutions & compliance leads to address your bullets. Quick summary of the proposed amendment and operational controls: 

- Amendment highlights (attached: redwood-eu-apac-amendment-v2.pdf):
  • EU-only storage for customer-submitted content (transcripts, fine-tune artifacts, logs) with KMS keys scoped to EU projects.
  • Explicit consent checkbox workflow if a customer wants to export content outside EU; that workflow stores a revokeable audit trail.
  • Data retention defaults aligned with Medivex policy; custom retention configurable per customer.

- APAC burst plan (attached spreadsheet):
  • Burst pool for Tokyo region with guaranteed baseline of 50 concurrent sessions and burst up to 200 on demand.
  • Routing policy: EU-origin requests remain pinned to EU unless originating session is explicitly created in APAC pilot cluster. Cross-region read-only telemetry will replicate to EU; write-mode metadata is restricted per amendment.
  • Failover play: incremental failover (per-route) — when APAC cluster is unavailable the request surface will fail back to EU pinned replicas; the failback process is automated but requires a 20-minute cooldown window to avoid event storms.

- Technical compliance note (Jonas Weber will follow up with a short checklist):
  • KV cache eviction guarantees during failover
  • KMS key ownership and HSM boundary description
  • Audit log retention and log-shipping controls

Next steps I propose: we finalize legal redlines on the amendment, Marcus prepares an order form for the renewed term (includes APAC burst SKU), and Laura will coordinate a short security call with Jonas.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
